s01.text: Attention stores a key and a value for every head, for every layer, for every token.

s02.text: That is a lot of duplication. Many heads end up storing almost the same key.

s03.text: Group-query attention says: keep all the queries separate, but let a group of heads share one key and one value.

s04.text: Eight query heads, one key and one value. Eight times less to store.

s05.text: And the query still gets to be its own self, so each head can still look somewhere different.

s06.text: Which sounds free. It is not, and the reason is a detail.

s07.text: The shared key has to serve eight different queries, so it has to be the average of what those eight heads wanted.

s08.text: Average keys are duller keys. The direction each head actually cared about gets smeared.

s09.text: So quality does drop. The question is how much, and how fast it stops dropping.

s10.text: DeepSeek went further and compressed the cache into a low-rank latent space instead.

s11.text: Which gets the size down further, at the cost of rebuilding the keys on every step.

s12.text: So the ladder is: share the heads, then compress them, then quantise what is left.

s13.text: Every rung of that ladder is a trade, and the whole field is climbing it.
